summary: Two synthetic search aliases point 'hydraulic pump' at parts that are not hydraulic pumps. Spark's shopping recommender then offered a water pump for a failed hydraulic pump.

flows_into: backend/data/canonical/master/parts.json (aliases, common_names; exported from the graph)

validated: Applied to a copy of backend/data/canonical and checked with the canonical engine's offline validation: see the report printed by the correction check.
to_apply_with_authorization: 1. Graph (shared production AuraDB): MATCH (:Part {part_id: 'PRT-078'})-[r:HAS_ALIAS]->(:SearchAlias {alias_id: 'ALI-0353'}) DELETE r; the same for PRT-097 / ALI-0433. The two SearchAlias nodes can then be deleted or left unlinked. The canonical ingest never deletes, so this step is manual.
2. Re-export the parts dataset (python backend/scripts/canonical.py export --dataset parts) so parts.json matches the graph.
3. Remove ALI-0353 and ALI-0433 from the SYN_search_aliases sheet and from backend/graph/cypher/03_parts.cypher, so a rebuild cannot bring them back.
already_mitigated_in_code: app/agent/service.py _same_class: a part whose own name, category and subcategory lack the product-class words asked for is never offered, so the wrong aliases no longer produce a wrong recommendation.
